reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Department creation, commission transition, director, and compensation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1973 1st Ex. Sess. S.B. 1 § 8 through A.L. 2011 H.B. 464; Revisor's Note: salary adjustment index under § 105.005 printed in Appendix E). Creates the Department of Labor and Industrial Relations headed by the labor and industrial relations commission (Art. IV § 49); executes Type I transfer and abolition of the industrial commission; sets nomination and senate-confirmed appointment of the director as chief administrative officer; transitions industrial commission members as of May 2, 1974; sets base commission salary ($72,735 plus § 105.005 adjustment); bars board of rehabilitation pay as of May 2, 1974; authorizes director appointment of division heads; and construes the director as department head for Reorganization Act of 1974 § 1(6)–(9). Independent review revised heading to reflect the 1974 commission transition and compensation provisions (commission salary under § 105.005/Appendix E and May 2, 1974 bar on board of rehabilitation pay) without implying director or division-head salaries are set here.

headings.title: Type II transfer of division of employment security
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1973 1st Ex. Sess. S.B. 1 § 8 through A.L. 2011 H.B. 464). Transfers powers, duties, and functions of the division of employment security (chapter 288 and others) to the department by Type II transfer.

headings.title: Type II transfer of division of workers' compensation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1973 1st Ex. Sess. S.B. 1 § 8 through A.L. 2011 H.B. 464). Transfers powers, duties, and functions of the division of workers' compensation (chapter 287 and others) to the department by Type II transfer.

headings.title: Board of rehabilitation transfer and abolition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and source notes (L. 1973 1st Ex. Sess. S.B. 1 § 8 through A.L. 2011 H.B. 464). Transfers powers, duties, and functions of the board of rehabilitation (chapter 287 and others) by Type I transfer to the division of workers' compensation and abolishes the board of rehabilitation.

headings.title: Labor standards transfer and chapter 36 employee selection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and source notes (L. 1973 1st Ex. Sess. S.B. 1 § 8 through A.L. 2011 H.B. 464). Transfers previously Type I-transferred powers of the divisions of industrial inspections and mine inspections (chapters 286, 290, 291, 292, 293, 294, and 444) from the inspection section to the division of labor standards, and requires chapter 36 selection for employees performing Mine Safety and Health Act and Occupational Safety and Health Act duties (retaining archived source phrasing "occupational safety health act").

headings.title: Type II transfer of state board of mediation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and source notes (L. 1973 1st Ex. Sess. S.B. 1 § 8 through A.L. 2011 H.B. 464). Transfers powers, duties, and functions of the state board of mediation under chapter 295 and others to the department by Type II transfer.

headings.title: Chapter 36 selection for employment security employees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and source notes (L. 1973 1st Ex. Sess. S.B. 1 § 8 through A.L. 2011 H.B. 464). Requires all employees of the division of employment security to be selected in accordance with chapter 36.

headings.title: Human rights commission transfer and member appointments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and source notes (L. 1973 1st Ex. Sess. S.B. 1 § 8 through A.L. 2011 H.B. 464). Executes a Type III transfer of the Missouri Commission on Human Rights (chapters 213, 296, 314, and others) to the department and requires nomination of commission members by the director for gubernatorial appointment with senate advice and consent.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of all eight subsections, history note (L. 1973 1st Ex. Sess. S.B. 1 § 8 through A.L. 2011 H.B. 464), and Revisor's Note citing the § 105.005 salary adjustment index in Appendix E; verified all fingerprints. Checked Art. IV § 49 commission structure, May 2, 1974 transition and board of rehabilitation pay bar, Reorganization Act of 1974 § 1(6)–(9) construction, Type I/II/III transfers, archived "occupational safety health act" wording in subsection 5, and chapter 36 employee selection. Revised subsection 1 to capture commission transition and compensation accurately; retained subsections 2–8.

headings.title: Powers, jurisdiction, and duties of the commission
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, including subdivisions (1) through (13), and source notes (L. 1945 p. 1101 § 6 through A.L. 2011 H.B. 315; footnote * noting 'Word "and" does not appear in original rolls' in subdivision (12); cross-references to §§ 286.121 and 287.801). Enumerates 13 commission powers and duties: sue/be sued, judicially noticed seal, chapters 287 and 288 responsibilities, division rule approval/disapproval and 10-day filing rule, central statistical system (excluding confidential records) and combined employer reports, central payroll/accounting, publishing laws and non-internal rules for citizens, internal management and quasi-judicial regulations, hearings/witnesses/oaths/testimony, certifying official acts, biennial general assembly/governor reports in lieu of prior agency reports, employment security appeal clerk/stenographer, and other statutory duties. Independent review verified footnote * on subdivision (12) ("Word 'and' does not appear in original rolls") and archived cross-reference wording citing "director of division of workers' compensation, 286.121".

headings.title: Rulemaking compliance with section 536.024
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes (including A.L. 1995 S.B. 3 and H.B. 300 & 95, A.L. 2011 H.B. 315, and cross-references to §§ 286.121 and 287.801). Conditions effectiveness of any rule or portion of a rule promulgated under chapter 286 on promulgation pursuant to § 536.024.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of both subsections, subdivisions (1)(1)–(13), history note (L. 1945 p. 1101 § 6 through A.L. 2011 H.B. 315), footnote * on subdivision (12) ('Word "and" does not appear in original rolls'), and cross-references to §§ 286.121 and 287.801 (including archived "director of division of workers' compensation" phrasing); verified all fingerprints. Checked § 536.024 rulemaking condition and confidential-record exclusion. Retained both headings as accurate.

headings.title: Occupational injury, illness, and Atomic Energy Commission statistics
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1971 S.B. 362 § 1, A.L. 1980 H.B. 1266, H.B. 1396, A.L. 1981 S.B. 389, A.L. 1995 H.B. 300 & 95). Directs the director to compile or supervise compilation of occupational injury and illness statistics required by the U.S. Department of Labor under the Occupational Safety and Health Act of 1970, and statistics required of the division by the United States Atomic Energy Commission (retaining archived historical federal agency name and noting catchline/§ 286.060 cross-reference phrasing). Independent review revised heading to accurately reflect statistics required by the archived United States Atomic Energy Commission rather than generic atomic energy statistics.

headings.title: Commission administration of Occupational Safety and Health Act
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1971 S.B. 362 § 1 through A.L. 1995 H.B. 300 & 95). Charges the labor and industrial relations commission—designated by the governor as administering agency for the Occupational Safety and Health Act of 1970—with taking all possible steps necessary to comply insofar as applicable to Missouri (noting catchline still says "industrial commission" while body text specifies "labor and industrial relations commission").

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of both subsections and history note (L. 1971 S.B. 362 § 1 through A.L. 1995 H.B. 300 & 95); verified all fingerprints. Checked catchline ("industrial commission") versus subsection 2 body text ("labor and industrial relations commission") discrepancy and retained legacy "United States Atomic Energy Commission" and "the division" wording in subsection 1. Revised subsection 1 to accurately reflect Atomic Energy Commission statistics; retained subsection 2.
